title: Speed up the construction of typed container types

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Improves the speed when typed container types are constructed directly from the opcode.
- Slightly improves the speed of constructing typed container types when they are marshalled. It doesn't make encoding  faster, only decoding benefits here.

## Additional information

In the beginning https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122723 was the original PR, but instead of adding the overloads that accepts temporary `ContainerType` I decided to change the type from `const Variant &` to `const Ref<Script> &` directly, which is much simpler and easier to reason about.

Paired PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123791, they implement similar ideas, but don't depend on each other.

This only improves the speed of the opcodes:
- `OPCODE_CONSTRUCT_TYPED_ARRAY`
- `OPCODE_CONSTRUCT_TYPED_DICTIONARY`

Container types constructors still have the same speed.

### GDScript VM changes

Used the same method as `RequiredParam::_internal_ptr_dont_use` in `object.h` to stop it from creating a temporary `Ref<Script>`. It should be safe because we are accessing the `Script` that is already stored in `Variant`, so we know we don't need `init_ref()`.

## Benchmark

The results are in tables with numbers measuring `ns/op`. The number in the column indicate how many threads were used for that run, 0 is a main thread. Each run had the same workload that was split between all running threads (this simulates parallel workload). Only tested using release templates.

Compile command: `scons target=template_release optimize=speed accesskit=no use_llvm=yes linker=lld production=yes`

Project: [testthreads4.6_2026-09-26_17-47-06.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32679717/testthreads4.6_2026-09-26_17-47-06.zip)
